correctness.rationale: With t=sqrt(1-u^2) and s=sqrt((k+2)/k)/2 the scalar equation is (ks-2t)/(k+4)=t/(2sqrt(1-t^2)); the difference is strictly decreasing from positive to minus infinity, so there is exactly one admissible root. All edges of the displayed embedding have squared length one, including when k=1 and the peripheral simplex is a single point. Applied to its centered coordinates the Rayleigh bound gives lambda_2 V<=B for every feasible allocation. Substitution into the rates gives LQ=lambda Q_c in the odd, even and simplex directions using mu/s=-k/H and mu=-t/(2u). There are 1+1+(k-1) such independent modes; the two block traces are 2w_AB+k w_AC+2w_AX and (k+2)w_AC+2w_AX, both strictly greater than 2lambda, so the two other nonzero eigenvalues strictly exceed lambda. Summing weights gives lambda V_k, and tracing the embedding identity also gives lambda V, proving equality and the optimal B/V_k. The root gives u->1/sqrt(2); division in the stated budget expression yields k/2+7/2+2u+1/u+O(1/k), giving the claimed asymptotic.
residual_risks: Unnormalized Laplacian, unit masses and fixed topology/total conductance. The displayed optimizer's multiplicity is proved; uniqueness and multiplicity of all optimizers are not claimed.

value.rationale: The family isolates the competition between a dense core and two bottlenecks on distinct hubs. The exact evaluation specifies how to allocate a finite budget across all existing edge classes, shows that none need be dropped, and gives a sharp spectral benchmark with the Fiedler multiplicity and asymptotic scale. This is substantive graph-specific information not obtained merely by restating the SDP.
residual_risks: No extension is established to other leaf configurations, masses or discrete-time dynamics, and no full optimizer classification is claimed.
